outcome: Since 26 January 2024 one event bears on the problem: Yu, Yuan and Zhou (arXiv 2602.01820, 2 Feb 2026) prove an explicit bound #C(K) ≤ 10¹³·g⁸·min{1+5/(4√g), 1+3log g/g}^rk J(K) for curves of genus g ≥ 2 over number fields K, whose exponent is the Mordell–Weil rank of the Jacobian, so it does not give a bound in K and g alone; the K-and-g-only statement is not reached by any source found, and the rank-dependent uniform Mordell results (Dimitrov–Gao–Habegger 2020/21; Kühne 2021) predate the window.
problem_asks: Part by part: (1) for every number field K and every integer g ≥ 2, there exists a finite number N(K,g); (2) every smooth projective (algebraic) curve C of genus g defined over K has at most N(K,g) K-rational points; (3) N(K,g) depends only on K and g, not on the particular curve C. The statement implicitly quantifies over all K and all g ≥ 2. Finiteness of K-points on each individual curve is Faltings' theorem and is not what is asked; what is asked is that the bound be uniform over all curves of genus g over K. Because N is allowed to depend on K, a bound depending on K only through its degree [K:Q] (Pacelli's form) would fit the wording, but a bound depending on the Jacobian's Mordell–Weil rank (Mazur's conjecture B form, N(K,g,r)) would not.

events.what_happened: Caporaso, Harris and Mazur, 'Uniformity of rational points', J. Amer. Math. Soc. 10 (1997) 1–35 (DOI 10.1090/S0894-0347-97-00195-1, as listed in the Wikipedia article's references). They show that a uniform bound N(K,g) would follow from the Bombieri–Lang conjecture (Wikipedia's wording); Abramovich's 1995 abstract describes the assumption as Lang's conjecture together with CHM's own 'Conjecture H'. The 1997 paper itself was not opened; the description comes from the Wikipedia article and from the later abstracts of Abramovich and Pacelli. An earlier preprint, if one exists, was not located.
events.revisions: Corrected by the authors in arXiv 2012.14461 (28 Dec 2020); see event chm-corrections-2020.
events.delivers: Conditional only. If the Bombieri–Lang conjecture holds (Lang's conjecture plus Conjecture H in Abramovich's account), then for each number field K and genus g there is a bound on the K-rational points of genus-g curves over K depending on g and K. Unconditionally, nothing.
events.remains: The unconditional bound N(K,g) for every number field K and every genus g ≥ 2.

checked_by.who: Journal of the American Mathematical Society (refereed journal of record)
checked_by.qualification: Peer review by the journal; referees are not named in the sources
checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted and published the paper. No independent verification was found.

events.time_since_posted: Not applicable: published 1997; the authors themselves issued a correction in 2020.
events.doubts: The authors' own 2020 correction says the 1997 paper 'corrects an error in the authors' earlier work, by proving stronger forms of the basic lemmas' (arXiv 2012.14461). So the conditional argument rests on a corrected version. The abstract of the correction does not say whether the error changed the conclusion or only the proof of the lemmas, and the full text was not read.
events.direction: Supports the bullet's uniform bound, but only conditionally, on Bombieri–Lang (or Lang's conjecture plus Conjecture H).

events.what_happened: Dan Abramovich, 'Lang's conjectures, Conjecture H, and uniformity', arXiv alg-geom/9505020 (submitted 21 May 1995, math.AG). Shows that Conjecture H of Caporaso–Harris–Mazur together with Lang's conjecture (non-Zariski-density of rational points on varieties of general type) implies uniformity of rational points on varieties of general type, as predicted by CHM. Per the Wikipedia article's summary, the argument gives a bound that stays bounded as the number field varies over quadratic extensions. Read from the arXiv abstract page only.
events.delivers: Conditional only. Conjecture H plus Lang's conjecture gives uniformity for varieties of general type, which includes the curves of genus g ≥ 2 in the bullet. Per the Wikipedia summary, the bound stays bounded across quadratic number fields. Unconditionally, nothing.
events.remains: The unconditional bound N(K,g) for every number field and every genus.
events.time_since_posted: About 31 years. Extended by Pacelli (1996) and cited by the Wikipedia article. No independent verification was found.
events.direction: Supports the bullet's uniform bound, but only conditionally, on Lang's conjecture plus Conjecture H.

events.what_happened: Patricia L. Pacelli, 'Uniform boundedness for rational points', arXiv alg-geom/9601004 (submitted 5 January 1996, one version). Assuming Lang's conjecture, she proves that for a number field K of fixed degree d, smooth curves of genus g > 1 over K have a number of K-rational points bounded by a constant depending only on g and d (per the abstract). Theorem 1.1 was not read; the abstract page was the only source. The paper extends Abramovich's result.
events.delivers: Conditional on Lang's conjecture: a bound on K-rational points of genus-g curves depending only on g and the degree [K:Q] (not on K beyond its degree). Per the Wikipedia article's summary, Pacelli's Bombieri–Lang version gives the same dependence. Unconditionally, nothing.
events.remains: The unconditional bound N(K,g). The conditional bound already has the form N(K,g) = B(g,[K:Q]), which fits the bullet's wording if the conditional hypothesis is granted.
events.time_since_posted: About 30 years. Cited in the Wikipedia article and in survey notes (Poonen's notes, cited as Pac97). No independent verification was found.
events.direction: Supports the bullet's uniform bound conditionally, with dependence only on g and degree.

events.what_happened: Conceição, Ulmer and Voloch (names as given in a search summary, not checked against the arXiv listing), 'Unboundedness of the number of rational points on curves over function fields', arXiv 1204.2001 (April 2012). Per the search summary, they construct sequences of smooth non-isotrivial curves of every genus at least 2 over a rational function field of positive characteristic whose numbers of rational points cannot be uniformly bounded. Not opened; the description comes from search snippets and from the Ulmer–Voloch 2016 abstract, which refers to 'counterexamples for a uniform boundedness question' over function fields.
events.delivers: Analogue only. Over function fields of positive characteristic the uniform bound fails. This says nothing about number fields, which is the bullet's setting.
events.remains: The number-field question, which is the bullet.
events.time_since_posted: About 14 years. Cited by the 2016 Ulmer–Voloch abstract.
events.direction: Against the function-field analogue. It does not decide the number-field question, which is the bullet.
events.object: Sequences of smooth non-isotrivial curves of each genus at least 2 over a rational function field of positive characteristic, with unbounded numbers of rational points (per search summary; the explicit families were not read).

events.what_happened: Douglas Ulmer and José Felipe Voloch, 'On the number of rational points on special families of curves over function fields', arXiv 1612.04325 (submitted 13 Dec 2016; v2 14 Dec 2016 with typo corrections). They construct families of curves that are counterexamples to a uniform boundedness question over function fields, generalising earlier families, and they show what fails in the Caporaso–Harris–Mazur argument that uniform boundedness follows from Lang's conjecture. Abstract read only.
events.delivers: Analogue only. Over function fields the uniform bound fails in the constructed families, and the CHM implication from Lang's conjecture cannot be run as originally argued there. This is not a result over number fields.
events.remains: The number-field question, which is the bullet.
events.time_since_posted: About 10 years. Its engagement with the CHM argument is noted in the Wikipedia article's discussion of function fields.
events.direction: Against the function-field analogue. Its explanation of where the CHM argument fails is relevant when weighing the conditional route, but it does not decide the number-field case.
events.object: Families of curves over function fields for which the number of rational points is not uniformly bounded, with explicit bounds on the heights and numbers of the points (abstract). The families themselves were not read.

events.what_happened: F. Pazuki, 'Theta height and Faltings height', arXiv 0907.1458 (submitted 9 July 2009; v2 30 June 2015). Compares the theta height and stable Faltings height of a principally polarised abelian variety and, under a conjecture of S. Lang and J. Silverman (a conjectural lower bound for heights), gives an explicit upper bound on the number of K-rational points of a curve of genus g > 1 over a number field K. Published Bull. Soc. Math. France 140 (2012) 19–49 per a search summary. The abstract page was read; the bound's formula was not.
events.delivers: Conditional on the Lang–Silverman-type height bound: an explicit bound on K-points of genus-g curves over K. Per search summaries the bound involves the Jacobian's theta height and Mordell–Weil rank; the formula was not read. Unconditionally, nothing.
events.remains: An unconditional bound, and the bullet's N(K,g) unless the conditional height bound is established.

events.what_happened: Michael Stoll, 'Uniform bounds for the number of rational points on hyperelliptic curves of small Mordell–Weil rank', arXiv 1307.1773 (v1 submitted 6 July 2013; v6 revised 25 Nov 2015); J. Eur. Math. Soc. 21 (2019) 923–956. For a hyperelliptic curve C of genus g over a number field K whose Jacobian has Mordell–Weil rank r ≤ g−3, the number of K-rational points is bounded in terms of g, r and [K:Q]; for K = Q the explicit bound is 8rg + 33(g−1) + 1. The proof is a refinement of Chabauty's method with a p-adic annulus estimate. Abstract page read; the explicit formula is from the search summaries and the abstract.
events.revisions: v6 25 Nov 2015 (shown on the arXiv page). Published JEMS 2019.
events.delivers: Unconditional, for hyperelliptic curves with Mordell–Weil rank r ≤ g−3: a bound in terms of g, r and [K:Q]. Restricted to hyperelliptic curves and small rank. Because the bound depends on r, it is Mazur's rank-dependent form (conjecture B) for that class, not the bullet's K,g-only bound.
events.remains: Non-hyperelliptic curves, ranks r ≥ g−2, and the bullet's K,g-only bound.

events.what_happened: Eric Katz, Joseph Rabinoff, David Zureick-Brown, 'Uniform bounds for the number of rational points on curves of small Mordell–Weil rank', arXiv 1504.00694 (submitted 2 April 2015; v3 6 Jan 2017); Duke Math. J. 165 (2016) 3189–3240. For a curve X of genus g ≥ 2 over a number field F of degree d with Mordell–Weil rank r ≤ g−3, the abstract claims an explicit uniform bound on #X(F). Methods: Chabauty–Coleman, Berkovich curves and metric graphs. Abstract page read only; the exact dependence of the bound on g, r and d was not read.

events.what_happened: L. Alexander Betts, David Corwin, Marius Leonhardt, 'Bounds on the Chabauty–Kim locus of hyperbolic curves' (first posted as 'Towards uniform Chabauty–Kim'), arXiv 2206.11085 (June 2022; revised October 2023); Int. Math. Res. Not. 2024 (no. 12, pp. 9705–9727, DOI 10.1093/imrn/rnae067) per search summary. Per the search summary, gives an explicit bound on the number of rational points of a genus ≥2 curve over Q depending on a prime p, the genus, the Mordell–Weil rank and the reduction types, conditional on the Tate–Shafarevich and Bloch–Kato conjectures. Not opened; description from a search snippet and summary.
events.revisions: Revised October 2023 (per search summary). Journal publication in IMRN 2024 falls inside the window, but the event date is the first public argument.
events.delivers: Conditional per the search summary; over Q only; depends on the Mordell–Weil rank and bad reduction types, so it is not a bound in g alone.
events.remains: The bullet's N(K,g) for number fields K other than Q, the rank-free and unconditional case, and the K,g-only form generally.
events.time_since_posted: About 4 years. Journal publication in IMRN 2024. No independent verification found.
events.direction: Rank-dependent bound over Q, conditional. Does not give the bullet's K,g-only bound.

events.what_happened: Vesselin Dimitrov, Ziyang Gao, Philipp Habegger, 'Uniformity in Mordell–Lang for curves', arXiv 2001.10276 (submitted 28 Jan 2020; v2 14 Jan 2021; v3 31 Mar 2021, appendix B revised); Annals of Mathematics 194 (2021) 237–298 (received 11 Feb 2020, accepted 30 Mar 2021, published online 23 June 2021 per the Annals page). For a smooth geometrically irreducible projective curve of genus g ≥ 2 over a number field of degree d, the number of K-rational points is bounded only in terms of g, d and the Mordell–Weil rank ρ of the Jacobian (search summary of Theorem 1.1: c(g,d)^(1+ρ)). Answers Mazur's question affirmatively. Also gives bounds in g and d for geometric torsion points. Method: Vojta's approach with a generalised height inequality. Abstract and Annals page read; full text not read.
events.revisions: v2 14 Jan 2021; v3 31 Mar 2021 (appendix B revised; accepted to Annals).
events.delivers: Unconditional rank-dependent uniform bound: depends on g, d and the Jacobian's rank ρ. It does not give a bound depending on K and g alone, because ρ is not bounded over genus-g curves over K.
events.remains: The bullet's N(K,g). That needs a bound on the Mordell–Weil rank of Jacobians of genus-g curves over K in terms of g and K, which no source found establishes. The rank-bound question is discussed in the Mazur/PPVW literature (search summaries), and conditional family results exist (Salami 2025).

events.what_happened: Lars Kühne, 'Equidistribution in families of abelian varieties and uniformity', arXiv 2101.10272 (submitted 25 Jan 2021; v2 3 Feb 2021; v3 5 Sep 2021; v4 23 Dec 2024). Using equidistribution in Arakelov theory with the Dimitrov–Gao–Habegger results, obtains uniform bounds. The abstract (as summarised by the abstract page) says the number of torsion points on a smooth genus-g curve in its Jacobian is bounded in terms of g alone, and that the number of rational points of a smooth curve over a number field 'can be bounded solely in terms of its genus and the Mordell–Weil rank of its Jacobian'. Abstract page read only; journal not found.
events.revisions: v2 3 Feb 2021; v3 5 Sep 2021; v4 23 Dec 2024 (inside the window; a revision, not a new event).
events.delivers: Unconditional, rank-dependent: a bound in terms of genus and Mordell–Weil rank (as the abstract summary states). The summary's wording omits the field degree, which DGH's bound includes; the full statement was not read, so the degree-free reading is recorded as the abstract's wording and not confirmed.
events.remains: The bullet's K,g-only bound, since the rank remains in the bound.
events.time_since_posted: About 5 years. Cited by Yu–Yuan–Zhou (2026), which describes Kühne's method and notes its constants are not explicit.
events.direction: Unconditional, rank-dependent. The bullet's K,g-only form is not reached.

events.what_happened: Ziyang Gao, Tangli Ge, Lars Kühne, 'The Uniform Mordell–Lang Conjecture', arXiv 2105.15085 (submitted 31 May 2021; v2 24 July 2021; v3 26 June 2024; v4 26 March 2026). Abstract (v4): proves a uniform version of the Mordell–Lang conjecture for subvarieties of abelian varieties in which 'the number of cosets necessary does not depend on the ambient abelian variety', via a gap principle that extends the DGH/Kühne curve gap principle; the gap principle implies the uniform Bogomolov conjecture in abelian varieties. arXiv comment: 'Accepted to Publications mathématiques de l'IHÉS'. Abstract page read only; the main theorem was not read.
events.revisions: v2 24 Jul 2021; v3 26 Jun 2024; v4 26 Mar 2026 (inside the window). Journal listing: PMIHES (per the arXiv comment; a search summary gives DOI 10.5802/pmihes.26, not verified).
events.delivers: Unconditional uniform Mordell–Lang statement for subvarieties of abelian varieties. The coset count is independent of the ambient abelian variety (v4 abstract). The abstract states no curve-level bound on rational points in terms of K and g, so this event does not establish the bullet's bound.
events.remains: The bullet's K,g-only bound for curves over number fields.
events.time_since_posted: About 5 years. Accepted by PMIHES per the arXiv comment.
events.doubts: Version drift: a search summary described v3 as stating the coset count does not depend on the ambient variety, and described v4 as depending on dimension and degree. The current v4 abstract, as read, says it does not depend on the ambient abelian variety. The record follows the v4 abstract. The theorem's exact dependence was not read.
events.direction: Unconditional uniform Mordell–Lang in abelian varieties. Does not state the bullet's curve-level bound.

events.what_happened: Tangli Ge, 'Uniformity of quadratic points', arXiv 2105.15090 (May 2021; an arXiv v2 exists). Per a search summary, extends the Dimitrov–Gao–Habegger uniformity to dimension two: a bound on quadratic points of non-hyperelliptic, non-bielliptic curves depending on the rank, the genus and the degree (form c^(1+ρ)); arXiv v1 states genus g ≥ 2 and the published version states g ≥ 3. Published Int. J. Number Theory 2024 per a search summary (journal date is not the event date). Not opened.
events.revisions: arXiv v2 exists (listing). Published IJNT 2024 (per search summary).
events.delivers: Analogue only: bounds the number of quadratic points on a restricted class of curves, not the K-rational points of all genus-g curves over K. It settles nothing about the bullet.
events.remains: The bullet.
events.time_since_posted: About 5 years. Published 2024 (per search summary).
events.direction: Analogue (quadratic points, restricted class). Does not decide the bullet.

events.what_happened: Sajad Salami (sole author; Universidade Estadual do Rio de Janeiro per a search summary), 'On the Rank of Jacobian Varieties of the Curves y^s = ax^r + b', arXiv 2510.27109 (submitted 31 Oct 2025; one version). Assuming the strong form of Lang's conjecture on varieties of general type, the Mordell–Weil ranks of the Jacobians of curves y^s = ax^r + b over a number field k (r, s ≥ 2 fixed; curves of genus ≥ 1) are uniformly bounded. Method: a parameter space for curves with a given number of rational points, whose fibres are complete intersection curves of increasing genus. Abstract page read; the body was not read; no journal publication found.
events.delivers: Conditional on Lang's strong conjecture: uniform bound on Mordell–Weil ranks of Jacobians for one family, y^s = ax^r + b. It is about rank in one family, not about K-rational point counts for all genus-g curves. Unconditionally, nothing.
events.remains: Rank bounds for other families and for all genus-g curves over K; the rational-point bound; the bullet.
events.time_since_posted: About 11.5 months (to 10 Oct 2026). No journal publication or independent engagement found.
events.doubts: Sole author; a single unrefereed arXiv posting found; conditional on Lang's strong conjecture, which is itself open. The argument is only sketched in the abstract (parameter space, fibres) and was not checked.
events.direction: Conditional rank-boundedness for one family. Does not reach the bullet's rational-point bound.

events.what_happened: Sajad Salami (sole author), 'Rank of Jacobian Varieties of Curves y^s = x(ax^r + b)', arXiv 2511.07680 (submitted 10 Nov 2025; one version). Assuming the strong form of Lang's conjecture concerning rational points on varieties of general type, the Mordell–Weil ranks of the Jacobians of curves y^s = x(ax^r + b) (a, b in k, ab ≠ 0, r ≥ 1, s ≥ 2, genus ≥ 1) over a number field k are uniformly bounded. Extends the earlier family result (2510.27109) by the geometric method of Yamagishi; the genus-one case y² = x(x²+B) has uniformly bounded rank under the same conditional hypothesis. Abstract page read; body not read.
events.delivers: Conditional on Lang's strong conjecture: uniform bound on Mordell–Weil ranks for the family y^s = x(ax^r + b), including the genus-one curves y² = x(x²+B). It is about ranks in a family, not about K-rational point counts for all genus-g curves. Unconditionally, nothing.
events.remains: Rank bounds outside this family; the rational-point bound; the bullet.
events.time_since_posted: About 11 months (to 10 Oct 2026). No journal publication or independent engagement found.
events.doubts: Sole author; a single unrefereed arXiv posting found; conditional on Lang's strong conjecture. The argument was not checked.
events.direction: Conditional rank-boundedness for one family. Does not reach the bullet's rational-point bound.

events.what_happened: Jiawei Yu, Xinyi Yuan, Shengxuan Zhou, 'Quantitativity on the number of rational points in the Mordell conjecture', arXiv 2602.01820 (v1 submitted 2 Feb 2026, math.NT; only version listed). Theorem 1.3: for a curve C of genus g ≥ 2 over a number field K with Jacobian J, #C(K) ≤ 10¹³ · g⁸ · min{1 + 5/(4√g), 1 + 3log g/g}^(rk J(K)). The constant depends on g; the exponent is the Mordell–Weil rank rk J(K). Theorem 1.6 (bad reduction, via Rémond's rank bound) and Theorem 1.7 (hyperelliptic discriminants) are consequences in which degree and height appear. The paper claims the base c₂(g) → 1 as g → ∞, answering a question of Gao and Habegger (per the introduction as read). Full HTML text read in two chunks; no acknowledgement or statement of AI or software use appears in the text read; acknowledgements thank Pascal Autissier and cite NSFC grants, the Xplorer Prize, China–Russia Mathematics Center and LabEx CIMI.
events.delivers: Explicit, unconditional, uniform in K for each fixed g. The bound is exponential in the Mordell–Weil rank of J(K), so it is rank-dependent. It does not give a bound depending on K and g alone, because the rank of J(K) is not bounded in terms of g and K by anything in the paper.
events.remains: The bullet's K,g-only bound. It would follow from a uniform bound on the Mordell–Weil rank of genus-g Jacobians over K, which the paper does not give and no source found establishes.
events.time_since_posted: About 8 months (posted 2 Feb 2026; checked 10 Oct 2026). No independent engagement found. The only later uptake found is a co-author's ICM survey (yuan-survey-2026) and seminar talk announcements from late 2025 to mid-2026, which are listings, not verification.
events.direction: Explicit, unconditional bound in terms of genus and rank. Cuts toward the rank-dependent uniform Mordell statement; it does not decide the bullet's K,g-only form.

events.remains: The bullet's K,g-only question, which the survey does not address in the abstract.

events.direction: Expository. Its use of 'solved' refers to the rank-dependent uniform Mordell problem, which bears on the naming dispute recorded in disputes.

events.what_happened: Lean formalisation work on Mordell's conjecture. The lean-lang.org evaluation page lists a Lean statement of Faltings' theorem, (h : 2 ≤ genus K F) implies the set of places of the function field with residue field rank 1 is finite, whose declaration uses sorry; no proof is present. Separately, a search summary of Michael Stoll's MIT talk (July 2024; PDF not readable) reports a plan to state Mordell's conjecture in Lean with the proof left as sorry. The statement is finiteness (Faltings), not the uniform bound.

events.what_happened: Press reports (Scientific American; magica.com; not opened) say that Levent Alpöge, described as working at Anthropic, and Ava Howell used Claude to present elliptic curves over Q of rank at least 30 and at least 31 within days of each other. A MathWorld entry (as of August 2026, per a search summary) treats the rank-30 lower bound as unconditional and describes the rank-31 claim as unverified. Magica reports a dropped witness point in the original rank-30 submission and no usable body for the rank-31 page. No arXiv preprint or author write-up was found.
events.delivers: Concerns genus-one curves: rank lower bounds from exhibited independent points. Nothing about genus ≥ 2 or the number of rational points. Discounted for this bullet. Recorded because uniform rank bounds are the gap that the bullet's K,g-only form would need closed.
events.remains: The whole bullet.
events.time_since_posted: Not established (exact date not found).

directly_checkable.what: Rank lower bounds are checkable by confirming that the exhibited points are independent (per Epoch's open-problem description as summarised).

events.doubts: Conflicting statuses: press reports the rank-31 record as Claude-assisted; MathWorld and Magica report one witness point dropped and no usable body for the rank-31 page.
events.direction: None for the bullet (genus one).

disputes.summary: Naming. The literature calls the rank-dependent statement the 'uniform Mordell' problem (Mazur's question as answered by DGH; 'uniform Mordell conjecture proposed by Mazur' in Yu–Yuan–Zhou's abstract). Yuan's 2026 survey says the uniform Mordell problem 'has been solved'. The Wikipedia article's lead, as fetched, states the K,g-only bound as the open problem and records no development after 2021. Whether 'solved' refers to the bullet's K,g-only statement is disputed in the sources themselves. Read against the explicit formulas, the solved statements are rank-dependent.

Caporaso–Harris–Mazur 1997 conditional bound: the authors concede in 2020 that the basic lemmas of the 1997 argument contained an error and replace them with stronger forms (arXiv 2012.14461). The abstract does not say whether the conditional conclusion survives unchanged.

Genus-one rank records credited to Claude (Alpöge and Howell). Press credits Claude; MathWorld and Magica describe the rank-30 bound as unconditional with a dropped witness point in the original submission, and the rank-31 page has no usable body. No author account was found, so no AI system is entered in the record. The dispute is about the genus-one records, not about this bullet.

summary: Found: the problem's bullet asks for a bound N(K,g) depending only on K and g. Every unconditional result found bounds K-points in terms of genus and the Mordell–Weil rank of the Jacobian, not in terms of K and g alone. The in-window event is Yu–Yuan–Zhou (arXiv 2602.01820, 2 Feb 2026): Theorem 1.3 bounds #C(K) by 10¹³·g⁸·min{...}^(rk J(K)), explicit and uniform in K for fixed g, with an exponent that is the rank. Its full text was read in two chunks. No statement of AI or software use appears in it. Older unconditional rank-dependent results: Dimitrov–Gao–Habegger (arXiv 2020, Annals 2021; bound in g, d and rank ρ, answering Mazur's question), Kühne (2021, v4 Dec 2024; abstract says 'solely in terms of genus and the Mordell–Weil rank'; the degree is absent from that wording while DGH includes it, so this is recorded as the abstract's wording and not confirmed), and Gao–Ge–Kühne (2021, v4 Mar 2026; uniform Mordell–Lang in abelian varieties, coset count independent of the ambient variety; no curve-level bound stated on the abstract). Restricted unconditional results: Stoll (2013/2019) and Katz–Rabinoff–Zureick-Brown (2015/2016) for rank ≤ g−3; Betts–Corwin–Leonhardt (2022, IMRN 2024) conditional and over Q. The conditional route to the bullet's form: Caporaso–Harris–Mazur (1997; their basic lemmas conceded erroneous and corrected in 2020), Abramovich (1995) and Pacelli (1996), where Pacelli's conditional bound depends only on g and the degree, which fits the bullet's wording if the hypothesis (Lang's conjecture) is granted. Recent conditional rank bounds for one family (Salami, Oct and Nov 2025) are sole-author unrefereed arXiv preprints. Close calls the judging pass should weigh: (a) whether the rank-dependent results count for the bullet's K,g-only wording, which the sources' own 'uniform Mordell solved' usage bears on; (b) whether conditional results (CHM, Pacelli, Pazuki, Salami) count; (c) whether the restricted-rank results (Stoll, KRZB) count. AI search: 45 searches (one rate-limited) found no AI-credited work on this bullet. The nearest AI item is a press-only genus-one rank record credited to Claude (Alpöge and Howell), which bears on ranks in genus one, is not a system entry, and is recorded as discounted. Other AI-credited work found is on other problems (Erdős unit distance, Jacobian conjecture counterexample, Chowla's conjecture paper, cubic-surface Cassels–Swinnerton-Dyer) and does not concern this bullet. The Abel Prize 2026 citation was seen only in search snippets and does not refer to uniform bounds. Dataset-wide, the Wikipedia article as fetched still lists the K,g question as open with no developments after 2021 and does not cite Yu–Yuan–Zhou; this is a fact about uptake, not a classification.
competing_reading: Read the bullet as the 'uniform Mordell' problem as the 2026 literature names it (Mazur's question as answered by DGH and Kühne, with explicit constants by Yu–Yuan–Zhou, which Yuan's survey calls solved). On that reading the question has an unconditional affirmative answer from 2021, and the 2026 event is an explicit-constant follow-up, not a new resolution. The bullet's own wording, N(K,g) depending only on K and g, is the stronger rank-free form. Reading it as the 'uniform Mordell' statement requires a rank bound that no source found gives.
what_would_settle_it: (1) A uniform bound on the Mordell–Weil rank of Jacobians of genus-g curves over K in terms of g and K (uniform rank boundedness). Combined with DGH or Yu–Yuan–Zhou this would give N(K,g) directly. (2) Reading the full text of Kühne (arXiv 2101.10272, v4) to confirm whether its stated bound really lacks the field degree, which would be stronger than DGH. (3) The full text of Yuan's ICM survey (arXiv 2606.27129) or a statement by Yu–Yuan–Zhou on whether 'uniform Mordell' in their usage is the rank-dependent statement. (4) Full texts of CHM's 2020 corrections and Pacelli's Theorem 1.1, to see whether the corrected conditional theorem keeps the K-or-degree dependence.
